ledger.event: Both sibling seats were launched and both returned nothing written, and the defect is the launch line rather than the seat. qwen-code's --approval-mode defaults to requiring approval for every file edit and shell command; in print mode there is no terminal to approve, so every write is refused silently. The recipe in factory/tools/seat.mjs has never carried the flag, which means no seat this factory has launched from that line could write unless something else supplied it, and the failure is invisible until a seat tries. Both seats diagnosed it themselves and refused to fake a return, the F41 seat writing that the lane has no return to read and should be re-seated rather than reviewed, which is the behaviour the factory wants from a cheap seat and is worth recording as such. Spend pasted from node factory/tools/seatReturn.mjs meter: F40 27 requests, 958342 in, 31963 out; F41 24 requests, 705121 in, 15894 out; deepseek-flash on both, the meter agreeing with the launcher's claim, which is F38's check doing its job on a lane that never landed. Relaunch with --approval-mode yolo was refused by this session's tool policy as Create Unsafe Agents, and so was the safer --approval-mode auto, so under T35 the line went to the owner and was not retried a third time. The read-only pass was not free of value: the F41 seat independently verified that all five allowlist paths the envelope seeds are genuinely absent and that no sixth citation reds on a hand pass, naming factory/help.example.json as the file that exists where factory/help.json does not, and it named the trap owed at landing.

F41 landed from writer/F41 at 8ccc04d, fast-forward, APPROVED ON THE FIRST RETURN with no correction, which makes two such lanes in this factory and both were written to a dictating envelope that named its mutation. A record's citation is now checked rather than trusted: a backticked path a lane log cites resolves in the commit under test or sits in an allowlist of five with a one-line reason each, an allowlist entry that DOES resolve fails as a stale exemption, and a date field in decisions or the board ledger is never ahead of the UTC date read in the same act as the comparison, while prose is left unscanned so a record may narrate a date it does not claim. S18 absorbed as T76. Two things the control plane had to add to the lane's own evidence rather than take on trust. The date check has two halves and the lane proved one: UTC rolled to 2026-09-21 during the sitting, which is the very date the ledger row narrating the mis-dating mentions, so the tree's green did not prove that prose stays unscanned. Driven separately here and by the reviewer at 2099-01-01: the date in a ledger row's event stays green, the same date in that row's at field reds. That is S19's shape caught before it shipped rather than after.

F40 returned at d493c05 and the review says CORRECTIONS NEEDED after approving both acceptance items at the CLI, which is the seventh lane in a row where an independent review found a blocking defect the control plane's own verification had missed. Finding one is a coverage hole rather than a wrong answer: the lane correctly deleted base main's row-equality assertion, because that one reached the helper instead of the CLI, and replaced it with checks on the seat COUNT, on a pid being present and on rows 9001 and 9002 being absent. Nothing asserts the VALUE of a row's harness field, so replacing harness with a hardcoded goose in the shipping census block leaves node factory/tools/seat.mjs --self-test printing ok at exit 0 while the live census renders pid 8324's qwen seat as goose. Driven by the control plane after the review named it. That is D-59's family arriving by a new route: not an assertion built from the producer, but an assertion that simply stops short of the property, left behind when a correct deletion was not matched by a correct replacement. Finding two is the invented citation again, in the same sitting that absorbed S18 as T76: docs/log/f40.md says all twenty-one steps were green including step 13, which the envelope expected red while the envelope is live, and the envelope says nothing about step 13, nothing about redness and nothing about liveness. The history behind the sentence is real and belongs to F39, which landed that fix before F40 was issued. The lane log narrated from the sitting's memory rather than from its own envelope. T76 does not catch it and the control plane states that rather than implying the new trap covers it: T76 checks that a cited PATH resolves and that a DATE FIELD is not ahead of UTC, and a claim attributed to a document that the document does not make is outside both. Correction 1 takes the harness label and the sentence, and is the only correction this sweep-tier seat gets.

F42 and F43 issued together at base cafac16, the sitting's second pair of siblings, proved disjoint at the files before either envelope was written. F42 takes S19, the last open spark that had a lane, and it is a correction of a half-proved fix rather than new ground: F35 landed splitCheck as case-sensitive AND last-wins with a fixture for the first half only, so restoring first-match while keeping case-sensitivity leaves the self-test green. The envelope therefore dictates a mutation PER ITEM that reds for that item alone, and says so in those words, because a single mutation that reds two items leaves one untested. It also takes the two gaps F35 named and did not take: a quoted YAML scalar carrying its quote characters into the id, the kind and the title, which YAML permits a child to write anywhere, and a child's kind of reject being mapped to portable so an explicit do-not-absorb signal is inverted into a candidate intake. F43 exists because this sitting paid for it twice. Both seats were launched from the qwen-code recipe exactly as written, and both read their packet, analysed correctly and wrote nothing, because that harness defaults to requiring approval for every edit and shell command and a print-mode seat has no terminal to approve at. The recipe has never named a mode, so no seat launched from that line could ever write. F43 names the mode on the one harness whose help output the control plane actually ran, and DICTATES that the three uninstalled harnesses declare the gap instead of guessing, because a guessed flag fails silently in exactly the way the qwen line just did and T07 is the trap for a recipe remembered rather than read. Two things about the issuance itself belong in the record. The tool policy refused to write F43's envelope through a shell heredoc, reading the flag named in the prose as an attempt to create an unsafe agent; the envelope was written with a file tool instead and its text now describes the option rather than spelling it, which is a constraint on how this control plane can document a launch line, not a safety judgement about the lane. And the seat packet went over its 26 KB cap again on the Now line and was compacted three times to 1471 characters to fit, which is the fourth time this sitting that the board's own prose has been the binding constraint on a writer's context.

F42 and F43 both returned CORRECTIONS NEEDED on the same shape, and the control plane's own envelopes are the cause, which is D-62. D-61 had already narrowed the rule to: an acceptance item names its mutation at the production entry point. Both envelopes obeyed it and both still let an untested property ship, because the rule counts mutations per ITEM and an item can carry several properties. F42's item 3 carried three: a reject row is held, the match is case-insensitive, and the refusal is read before the floors. One mutation was named, the first was proved, and the control plane drove the other two itself after the review named them: dropping the toLowerCase in portableOf, and swapping the refusal check to sit after the check floor, each leaves alumni --self-test printing ok at exit 0, because the only reject fixture is already lowercase and already clears every floor. That is precisely the defect F42 existed to correct in F35, reproduced one level up by the envelope that ordered the correction. F43's item 3 carried a scope claim, every recipe the list command prints, and the implementation read scope as every recipe rendering a stdin carrier; the envelope's own words, its carrier line, invited that. goose renders no carrier, a property that predates the lane, so goose is invisible to the check while being one of the three recipes item 2 names, and deleting goose's unverified note leaves seat --self-test green while the same deletion on aider or opencode correctly reds.

F43 landed from writer/F43 at 75f5d1d, fast-forward, after one correction, and it closes every lane booked this sitting. A print-mode launch line now names the harness's approval mode, absorbed as T80, and the lane exists because this sitting paid for it twice: two seats were launched from a recipe that had never named one, and both read their packet, did correct work in their heads and wrote nothing, because the harness default requires approval for every edit and shell command and a print-mode seat has no terminal to give it. The correction is where the lane got better than its envelope. The control plane dictated only that scope stop being the stdin carrier, which had made goose invisible to the check while being one of the three recipes the envelope named. The seat delivered that and two things nobody asked for: it strips the unverified declaration out of the text before testing whether a recipe is in scope, so the declaration cannot pull its own recipe into or out of the rule, which is the circularity the rescoping invited; and it asserts the in-scope set is non-empty, so the whole rule cannot pass by covering nothing. Both are the D-62 question asked unprompted, and they are the first time this sitting a sweep seat has closed a hole the envelope did not name. Four mutations driven by the control plane at the objects, each naming its own recipe: goose, aider and opencode each red on their note being stripped where goose was green before the correction, and the qwen carrier reds naming both qwen-code and its desktop-qwen alias. git range-diff proves all three commits replayed identically across the rebase main's own movement forced. Spend recorded as row 3662c93dcb6ac0de: 46 requests, 2885716 in, 77885 out, 2793472 cached, deepseek-flash, meter agreeing with the launcher, 96.8 per cent of input carried by cache. The lane's own log carries a finding the control plane is keeping rather than waving through: the gate reported all 21 steps red inside the seat, the seat ran a control at live main's tip, got the same 21 reds, concluded the red was not its own and handed classification up rather than guessing. That is the behaviour to keep. The cause is the seat's bash resolving to the WSL launcher, the same gate passing 21 of 21 from git-bash at the same commit, and it makes a sentence in T70 false. S24.

F44 and F45 issued together at base ab398c3, proved disjoint, and they take two of the four sparks that ended this sitting's booked work with no lane. F44 takes S22: the census counts processes rather than seats, six rows for two launches, and F40 landing did NOT fix it because every one of those rows carries the harness token in program position, so T77 names it as a limit and this lane closes it by folding a launch's process tree through the parent pid the lister already can report. F45 takes S23, the one that cost a paid session here: a correction envelope is written to main while a seat reads its envelope from its own worktree, which still sits at the issuance commit holding the superseded page, and git fetch does not touch the working tree. The seat path will refuse and write NOTHING to stdout, because the launch line is a pipe into the harness and an empty stdin is a loud failure, while a comparison that cannot be made is a NOTE and not a refusal, since a check that cannot pass is T09 and this factory has shipped one before. F45 is the delicate one and the envelope says so: the gate runs packet.mjs from an unpacked archive with no git, CI checks out shallow, and F31's byte-stable prefix is a 95 to 97 per cent cache hit this sitting, so nothing the lane adds may reach stdout in any path. Issuing the pair put the seat packet over its 26 KB cap again and the shed was found where D-58 says to look before firing its trigger. The traps digest had grown from 11.4 KB to 12.3 as this sitting wrote five trap rows, and a rule that names a check compresses to its FIRST SENTENCE, so four rules from the previous sitting, T72 T73 T74 and T75, were carrying 200 to 256 characters of evidence into every seat's digest because each was written as one sentence with no internal period. Splitting the rule from its evidence in each took the packet from 100.1 per cent to 97.8 while traps.yaml GREW to 22925 bytes. That is the second time this sitting the same mechanism has paid: detail written for a person reading the file costs a seat nothing, and per-lane scoping stays deferred with its trigger unfired.

F44 returned at 2d79199 and the review says CORRECTIONS NEEDED, having approved the fold and then found two failures neither the envelope nor the control plane had named, both driven again by the control plane at the objects. The walk assumes the process listing is a complete, acyclic, single-instant snapshot in which every ancestor pid resolves to a row, and on this machine that is false twice: Windows stamps ParentProcessId at creation and never clears it when the parent dies, and Get-CimInstance does not enumerate atomically. First, two counted rows whose parent pids point at each other, which ordinary pid-reuse churn produces, each fold into the other and BOTH vanish: the census prints 0 running writer seats for two live harness processes. That is worse than the over-count this lane exists to fix, because the two-writer ceiling and the dead-seat resume read this number, so a false zero lets a third seat launch and lets a resume collide with a session still running. Second, a counted row whose parent is absent from the listing, having exited between the enumeration and the write, cannot be attached to its launch and is counted as a second seat, which is precisely the S22 shape the lane was issued to close, reopened by churn rather than by any path the two required mutations touch.

F45 returned at 7a828e5 and the review says CORRECTIONS NEEDED on a defect worse than the one the lane closes. The two new fixtures cover no repository at all, and a repository whose copies DIFFER. Neither covers the case every ordinary launch takes, where the comparison succeeds and the copies are IDENTICAL, so that branch has no fixture that could fail it. Driven by the control plane at the objects: replacing if (same) return null with if (false) return null leaves packet --self-test printing ok at exit 0, while packet seat F45 on a clean byte-identical worktree exits 3 with ZERO bytes on stdout and refuses. Every lane, every worktree, with no correction pending, would refuse and no seat could launch, and the self-test, the check and the landing gate would all stay green. That is exactly what T09 and the envelope's own item 2 forbid, and the envelope is the cause: it named three mutations, drop the refusal, make the unresolvable case refuse, and leak the note to stdout, and never named the equality comparison itself as a property. D-62 for the third and fourth time in one sitting, now in both siblings at once. The review also found the log claiming sizeBudget printed 70 budgets where it prints 71, every KB and percent figure beside it being correct, which is the fourth uncommanded count this sitting. What the review cleared, having driven it: the refusal writes nothing to stdout and exits 3 naming the difference and the remedy, an unresolvable comparison notes and emits proved from an unpacked archive with no git, stdout is byte-identical between the two paths at 32226 bytes, and the gate is 21 of 21.

F45 landed from writer/F45 at 8d14688, fast-forward, after one correction plus a control-plane documentation fix, and S23 is absorbed as T81. A seat now compares the envelope in its worktree with the copy on live main and refuses when they differ, writing NOTHING to stdout so the harness gets an empty stdin and dies loudly, while a comparison that cannot be made is a note that still emits, proved from an unpacked archive with no git. The correction is the one to read. The lane's fixtures covered no repository at all and a repository whose copies differ, and never the case every ordinary launch takes, where the copies are IDENTICAL. Forcing the comparison to report a difference left --self-test, the check and the landing gate ALL green while every lane and every worktree would refuse with zero bytes on stdout and no seat in the factory could launch. Driven by the control plane at the objects before the correction and after: it now names that an identical envelope was refused and a working launch killed, and both directions of the comparison have their own red. The envelope was the cause for the fourth time this sitting, having named three mutations and never the equality itself. Landing also cost a control-plane documentation fix rather than a second correction, and the reason is worth the room: the gate went red on T76, the trap F41 landed this same sitting to catch invented citations, because the log cited the git revision spec HEAD colon the packet path, which RESOLVES - git rev-parse prints the blob and it matches the hash the log pins - but T76 reads any backticked token with a slash and a source extension as a tree path. A true citation in a form this factory uses often was rejected by the trap written to protect citations. The seat's one correction was spent, so the control plane rewrote the line to cite the command instead, which AGENTS section 4 prefers anyway, and recorded that it did so. That false-positive class is S25. Spend recorded as row a387304fc267d8be: 33 requests, 2385838 in, 98563 out, 2220544 cached, deepseek-flash, meter agreeing with the launcher.
